text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD#84721 — high 95th-percentile latency on /v1/generate (us-west-2) :warning:
pagerduty-bot: Trigger: latency_95 > 1200ms for 3m (service: inference-runtime)
alex: acked. i'm on. pulling up dashboards now :eyes:
alex: quick look — p95 jump to ~1300ms, p99 ~2100ms, 5xx unchanged. traffic steady.
support-sam: any customer impact? tickets?
alex: no customer-facing 5xx spikes in the last 10m, no new support tickets in the queue. looks like latency-only.
maria: joining. any region-specific signal?
alex: only us-west-2 has the pronounced bump. other regions normal. KV cache miss rate increased in us-west-2 by ~30% at the same time.
incident-bot: runbook suggestion: check KV warmup, check node flaps, check autoscaler surge events.
alex: running quick checks. listing pods on inference workers in us-west-2:
```
kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=us-west-2 -o wide
kubectl logs -f svc/kv-cache -n infra --tail=200
```
alex: saw a couple of short-lived restarts on two worker pods ~2m ago, and the autoscaler fired a small scale-up then scale-down quickly. possible cold-cache warmup + transient CPU contention.
maria: that fits. anything that needs immediate mitigation? can we drain the noisy host or pin traffic to healthy pool?
alex: i can temporarily route eu traffic to fallback model in us-west-2, but want to avoid cross-region latency. better quick mitigation: temporarily enable prefix caching for common prompt hashes and bump the KV cache prewarm TTL. doing now.
alex: toggled TTL from 30s -> 120s for prefix cache (us-west-2) via infra flag.
maria: nice. monitor for 2m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty note: PD#84721 acknowledged by alex at 3301234575
(reacted by maria with :thumbsup:)
alex: after TTL bump, p95 trending down to ~900ms within 90s. p99 still noisy but improving.
support-sam: nothing customer-visible so far — recommend we mark as no-customer-impact for now and keep monitoring.
maria: agree. opening a short follow-up ticket for root cause analysis. assigning to me.
alex: alert auto-resolved (PagerDuty) at 3301234689 — metric returned below threshold for 4m.
pagerduty-bot: PD#84721 automatically resolved (status: resolved) — reason: metric below trigger.
incident-bot: auto-resolve detected. please confirm handoff and any follow-up actions.
maria: taking post-incident. planned follow-up: investigate autoscaler flapping threshold + KV cache prewarm behaviour, correlate with background eval jobs, add a suppression rule for short spikes under 3m, and update runbook with a TTL prewarm step.
alex: noted. i'll add the temporary TTL change and small runbook note to the ticket for traceability.
support-sam: i'll draft a short customer note template in case any ticket surfaces.
oncall-next: i'm on in 30m — i'll pick up final closure and ensure runbook updates land in the repo.
maria: thanks. quick action list: 1) RCA ticket created (#INC-2026) assigned to maria; 2) runbook update PR by alex; 3) suppression/alert tuning proposal by maria; 4) monitoring dashboard alert annotation (alex).
alex: sounds good. leaving note: no evidence of increased error rate or data loss. probable transient warmup after autoscaler churn.
maria: will look through kube events and the autoscaler logs, and check whether an internal eval job overlapped.
support-sam: marking as "no-customer-impact" for incident log. will keep watch.
incident-bot: thread closed for now. reopen if metrics regress. :white_check_mark:
